assertions.description: The feature: the WebSocket constructor must read a targetAddressSpace member from its options dictionary. Probed with a getter, so no connection or permission prompt is involved.
assertions.test: (()=>{let read=false;const url=new URL('/public/echo-socket',location.href);url.protocol=url.protocol==='https:'?'wss:':'ws:';try{const s=new WebSocket(url.href,{get targetAddressSpace(){read=true;return 'local';}});s.close();}catch(e){}return read;})()

assertions.description: fetch() has had the option for a while; WebSockets is catching up. Asserting the fetch side pins the reference point rather than assuming it, and shows the two are meant to match.
targetAddressSpace is an enum of loopback, local and public. A value outside it must be a TypeError at construction — a typo should be a bug you find, not a permission you silently never get.
assertions.test: (()=>{let read=false;const url=new URL('/public/echo-socket',location.href);url.protocol=url.protocol==='https:'?'wss:':'ws:';try{const s=new WebSocket(url.href,{get targetAddressSpace(){read=true;return 'somewhere-else';}});s.close();return false;}catch(e){return read?e instanceof TypeError:false;}})()

assertions.description: This option can only exist because the constructor takes a dictionary, so the two features are asserted together: if protocols is not read from a dictionary, targetAddressSpace cannot be either.
assertions.test: (()=>{let read=false;const url=new URL('/public/echo-socket',location.href);url.protocol=url.protocol==='https:'?'wss:':'ws:';try{const s=new WebSocket(url.href,{get protocols(){read=true;return [];}});s.close();}catch(e){}return read;})()

assertions.description: The control: a same-origin socket must still open normally. Without this the other assertions cannot be interpreted.
assertions.test: (async()=>{const url=new URL('/public/echo-socket',location.href);url.protocol=url.protocol==='https:'?'wss:':'ws:';return await new Promise((res)=>{let s;try{s=new WebSocket(url.href);}catch(e){return res(false);}s.addEventListener('open',()=>{s.close();res(true);});s.addEventListener('error',()=>res(false));setTimeout(()=>{try{s.close();}catch(e){}res(false);},4000);});})()
